problemStatement: Provide an HTTP service that maps long URLs to short, shareable codes and redirects visitors to the original URL, with optional custom aliases and expiry, durable SQLite storage, input validation, a health endpoint, automated tests and run documentation.
functionalRequirements: FR1: POST /api/links accepts a long URL and returns a short code plus the full short URL (201 Created).
FR2: GET /{code} redirects (302) to the original URL; unknown codes return 404.
FR3: Callers may supply a custom alias; a taken alias returns 409 Conflict.
FR4: Callers may supply an expiry timestamp; expired links return 410 Gone and past expiry on create is rejected.
FR5: GET /api/links/{code} returns link metadata; DELETE /api/links/{code} removes the link (204/404).
FR6: Only absolute http/https URLs are accepted; malformed or non-http(s) URLs return 400 with problem details.
FR7: GET /health returns 200 while the process is alive.
FR8: Links are persisted in SQLite and survive process restarts.
nonFunctionalRequirements: NFR1: Zero-step local setup - the database is created automatically on first start.
NFR2: Short codes are unpredictable (cryptographic RNG) and collision-safe (unique index + bounded retry).
NFR3: The service must not be usable to probe internal networks: loopback/private hosts are rejected by default.
NFR4: All error responses use RFC 7807 problem details.
NFR5: Automated tests run with `dotnet test` in under a minute without external services.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Creating a link for https://example.com/x returns 201, a 7-character Base62 code and a shortUrl ending in that code.
AC2: GET /{code} for a created link returns 302 with Location equal to the original URL.
AC4: POST with ftp://, javascript:, an empty string, a relative URL, a loopback host or embedded credentials returns 400.
AC5: Creating with customAlias 'my-alias' returns code 'my-alias'; creating again with the same alias returns 409.
AC6: A link whose expiresAt has passed returns 410 on redirect; creating with a past expiresAt returns 400.
AC7: DELETE removes the link so GET /api/links/{code} returns 404 afterwards; deleting again returns 404.
assumptions: A1: No authentication is required for the first version (public shortener); link deletion is unauthenticated and documented as such.
A2: 302 (temporary) redirects are used so analytics can be added later without browsers caching the redirect.
A3: A single-instance deployment with SQLite is acceptable for this iteration; horizontal scaling is out of scope.
outOfScope: Rate limiting and abuse protection beyond input validation
User accounts, API keys, link ownership

ambiguities.question: Should the same long URL always map to the same code (idempotent create) or create a new code each time?
options: Reuse existing code for identical URL
ambiguities.defaultAssumption: New code per request - simpler, avoids leaking that a URL was already shortened by someone else.

ambiguities.question: Which redirect status code: 301 (permanent, cacheable) or 302 (temporary)?
ambiguities.defaultAssumption: 302 so future analytics see every click.
